function: Joint LEO/GEO beam management (hopping, pointing, gain, power) by graph-attention DRL, and user access, channel allocation and power control by PPO, for interference avoidance (pp. 7-9).
system: Forward link: GEO satellite (7 beams) sharing spectrum with LEO satellites (12 beams), dish user terminals, OFDMA, Ka band 19 GHz; no RIS (pp. 4, 10).
method: Joint model-based and model-free DRL (JMBMF-DRL): heterogeneous-graph attention policy for beams plus PPO actor-critic for resources, trained by reinforcement learning with Adam (pp. 7-10).
data_channel: Own simulator: ITU-R P.618/P.676/P.840 attenuation and S.672-4 antenna model for GEO links; Rician (kappa=10) with free-space loss for LEO links; Starlink orbital data from CelesTrak (pp. 4, 10).
test_conditions: Trained 500 epochs of 100-step episodes in the simulated scenario; sweeps over SINR threshold, user distribution, terminals (20-80), LEO power (10-40 W); no train/test split stated (pp. 10-13).
baselines: Non-learned: random resource allocation (RRA); learned: standard PPO for beams and resources; ablation: JMBMF without beam hopping (pp. 11-12).
metrics: System throughput (Gbps), spectral efficiency (bps/Hz), SINR of GEO users (dB), training convergence (pp. 11-13).
complexity: Order of complexity O(NT(Theta0 Theta_l + sum Theta_l Theta_l+1) + |S||A|) from network size and action selection; no FLOPs or runtime reported (p. 10).
openness: none; Starlink orbital data come from public CelesTrak, but no code, channel data, or link is released (p. 10).
q1_support: p. 4: "recommendations of ITU-R P.530 [37]"; the GEO channel is built on ITU-R P.618, P.676, P.838, P.840 and S.672-4, while the LEO link is the paper's own Rician model, citing 3GPP TR 38.821 only as guidance.
q2_support: p. 13: "system throughput with different number of satellite terminals"; the agent is trained in the same simulated scenario (p. 10), and the paper never states that a trained model was tested on terminals, power, positions, or distributions not used in training.
q3_support: p. 11: "RRA (Random Resource Allocation)" is the non-learned baseline and "PPO (Proximal Policy Optimization)" the learned baseline; throughput and SINR are compared in Fig. 5 and Table II (p. 12).
q4_support: p. 10: "we provide a computational complexity analysis of" the proposed algorithm, giving its total order as O(NT(Theta0 Theta_l + sum Theta_l Theta_l+1) + |S||A|).
q5_support: p. 10: "The orbital data for Starlink is derived from CelesTrak." This is public orbit data, not a dataset of channels or signals, and no link to code or data appears anywhere in the paper.
notes: First page title matches the DOI. Tables I-II and Figs. 4-5 are images, read from pp. 10-12. q1 is flagged for the reviewer: ITU-R recommendations count as another standardized model, but the LEO link is a custom Rician model. q3 is flagged: PPO is also the model-free half of the proposed method, counted as a standard learning algorithm applied to the same problem. The learned user access choice is above the physical layer but is joint with beams, power and spectrum.
